name: Bio-LNG and liquefied biomethane
principle: Biogas is upgraded to biomethane, then liquefied with a small-scale liquefier to give a drop-in LNG substitute for heavy transport and shipping. Shell commissioned a bio-LNG plant of about 100,000 tonnes a year in April 2024 (location not confirmed by the page read).

performance.basis: Natural Gas World, April 2024; site and feedstock not stated in the text read

source.note: Natural Gas World, Shell inaugurates Germany's largest bio-LNG production plant, 19 April 2024

advantages: Counts as renewable fuel under many schemes (not checked)

reference_plants.name: Nordsol bio-LNG plant, Amsterdam (Nordsol/Shell/Renewi)
reference_plants.capacity: 3,400 t/yr bio-LNG plus 6,800 t/yr liquid bio-CO2; feedstock is biogas from Renewi waste processing; opened 15 Oct 2021 - the first bio-LNG plant in the Netherlands

source.note: Bioenergy news, 15 Oct 2021 (opening, 3.4 kt/yr, Nordsol-Shell-Renewi); Nordsol factsheet (European Biogas Association); read 2026-10-28

costs.basis: Greenville liquid biomethane plant; the capacity of the plant is not stated on the page, so this is a single unverifiable data point.

source.note: French Renewable Energy project page, read 2026-11-16

notes: Process provenance: the chain follows Nordsol's project description - anaerobic digestion, raw-gas dehumidification and H2S/VOC removal, bulk CO2 removal in a standard upgrading unit, membrane polishing with permeate recycle, liquefaction by reverse Brayton cycle with a single turboexpander, then cryogenic storage and truck loading, with biogenic CO2 capture. Digester design and detailed H2S removal are not covered.
